actual_checks: Full exact report, literal prompt, API/metadata, author/source records and both retained prior scientific bodies read. The new scope is the distinct-Hodge–Tate p>=5 two-dimensional odd Fontaine–Mazur case, with the modularity-to-geometric-realization bridge made explicit; prior potential-realization/finite-image arguments alone did not supply this theorem.

Pan Theorem 1.0.4 is applied with continuity, absolute irreducibility, finite ramification, oddness and potentially semistable distinct Hodge–Tate weights. Its extra residual restriction is only for p=3, correctly excluded here. Pan uses cyclotomic weight -1 and geometric Frobenius; weight/twist conventions are preserved.

Scholl realizes the cuspidal eigenform representation in smooth projective cohomology (weight 2 via a Jacobian, higher weight via Kuga–Sato and the indicated projector); duals are accommodated by Poincare duality and Tate twists. The scalar intertwiner character is de Rham and finite ramified; its cyclotomic adjustment has weight zero and hence finite image over Q by Sen and global class field theory.

The finite-image character is realized in degree-zero Artin cohomology and combined by Kunneth. A smooth projective possibly disconnected source can be embedded as a codimension-at-least-two center in projective space; the blowup is geometrically integral and its blowup formula supplies the shifted/twisted summand. Restriction of coefficients and Jordan–Holder descent give the stated irreducible subquotient without an unjustified semisimplicity assertion. The full Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, repeated weights and p=2/3 are not claimed.
